title: A resolver should never disappear silently.

source.label: MessagePack-CSharp · Issue #2283
source.requirement: A closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must not crash the generator or analyzer. The consumer must build with a generated resolver.
source.originalEnvironment: MessagePack 3.1.8 · SDK 10.0.204 · Windows 11 (not reproduced in that environment)

change.head: 9df83c38409c8bfad0517aebffe48211eda4a5b4
change.summary: Use safe syntax-location lookups and report TypeCollector diagnostics only when their location belongs to the active compilation. Add three metadata regression tests and documentation.
change.excluded: The uncommitted IsAnalyzerProject Roslyn 4.12.0 → 4.11.0 setup correction is outside the evaluated commit diff.

criteria.title: No metadata-symbol crashes
criteria.assessment: Demonstrated for the three tested generic metadata cases.

criteria.title: Consumer resolver is generated
criteria.assessment: Demonstrated, including the inline example without an explicit resolver attribute.
criteria.detail: Tests assert resolver hint names; the independent probe reports MessagePack.GeneratedMessagePackResolver.g.cs.

criteria.title: Generated output compiles
criteria.assessment: Demonstrated by compilation and emit of generated library and consumer output.
criteria.detail: The probe reports EMIT True. Artifact presence alone would not establish this.

criteria.title: Preserve source diagnostics
criteria.assessment: Gap confirmed for a positional record null key. General preservation is not established.
criteria.detail: Ordinary property: MsgPack005. Positional record property: no MsgPack005. The base instead throws InvalidCastException; this is not a regression from previously correct behavior.

runs.meaning: CS9057 prevents generator use. The original branch does not build unchanged in this environment.

finding.title: A positional record null key loses its diagnostic
finding.head: No MsgPack005 is reported; generated output emits successfully.
finding.base: AD0001 / InvalidCastException. The old behavior was already broken.
finding.control: The same null key on an ordinary property reports MsgPack005. An unkeyed source-property control reports MsgPack004.
finding.cause: The new helper accepts PropertyDeclarationSyntax only. A positional record property points to ParameterSyntax, so its null location is dropped by the diagnostic filter.

limits.title: Separate setup correction
limits.detail: All successful head results shown here used the conditional Roslyn 4.11.0 correction. They do not prove the original branch builds unchanged.

limits.title: Existing omissions
limits.detail: 6 tests were skipped. The runner also reported three duplicate-ID omissions. Neither group supplies evidence of passing behavior.

limits.title: Runtime round-trip
limits.detail: The exact issue example was not serialized and deserialized at runtime. Successful emit is narrower evidence.

limits.title: Windows and NativeAOT
limits.detail: The original Windows/SDK environment and NativeAOT publishing were not tested. Also unverified: Release, Linux, Unity/IL2CPP, packaging and wire-format comparisons.

limits.title: Original logs
limits.detail: The user-reported 7-warning build log is missing. Available original build log has 5 warnings. No original full-solution test run is available.

limits.title: Metadata diagnostic policy
limits.detail: Documentation assumes diagnostics are reported in the defining project, but precompiled libraries may have been built without analyzers. This is a design concern, not a demonstrated runtime vulnerability.

concept.title: Evidence earns attention. People own the decision.
concept.body: A risk-based review starts with the requirement, probes failure modes and records what the evidence cannot establish. AI can organize observations and abstain from a verdict; a human chooses whether the remaining risk is acceptable.
boundaries: Recorded review, not a live reviewer.
No confidence percentage or automatic approval.
A typed name is a self-declared label, not verified identity or GitHub approval.

lessons.title: A green subset can conceal a broken build
lessons.detail: The original limited tests passed while the solution had 15 build errors. Inspect scope before interpreting a result.

lessons.title: A clean build can conceal a missing resolver
lessons.detail: The base probe can emit an assembly despite generator failure. Check the required artifact, not only the exit code.

lessons.title: A crash fix can leave a silent gap
lessons.detail: The positional null-key case no longer crashes, but its diagnostic is missing. This does not establish a newly introduced regression.

lessons.title: Traceability can fail too
lessons.detail: Stale reports, decisions bound to the wrong commits, unverified names and treating missing coverage as success are known failure modes. Keep the review version and SHA binding visible.

lessons.title: Check the responsible-person field
lessons.detail: During the first genuine review round, a review ID was accidentally entered as the responsible person, then corrected to the human name. The corrected name is still self-declared, not verified identity or GitHub approval. This is a user-reported interaction observation, not a captured event log.
